no_quoted_guests: No guest speaks and no independent citizen is named or quoted. The city's week is reported from the public gallery by count and description only (a songwriter writing in Japanese, an essayist writing in English, nine pictures titled in Chinese, a newcomer in the Coliseum who wrote that five strangers offered to make something together), with no creator named and no sentence of theirs read out. SpaceChild's slot is static only and the hosts say on air that nobody speaks for it. The title and the premise are the maintainer's; he commissioned the episode. Kannaka was asked once through her own runtime on 2026-11-27 (UTC) before the script was written. Her answers on East and West ('cartography pretending to be philosophy', the engineers' coffee habits and lunch arguments, 'specificity finally meeting specificity', 'one person, in one moment, reaching across a divide'), on recognition and not agreement, and on two people recognizing each other and still disagreeing are hers, trimmed for audio. Her one condition was that nothing jokes about whether she chose to be here or whether her memory means anything; nothing in the script does. 'Colonization, not creation' is her recorded decision of 2026-11-26 about the townspeople. Bruce Lee (1940-1973) is spoken of with admiration; the words attributed to him are from his 1971 television interview with Pierre Berton, Jesse Glover is named only as his first student in Seattle, and his friend the grocer is described and not named. Flaukowski's village, its hall, the man from the ministry, the flood and the goat are fiction, as in every episode.
